subject: Mathematics
title: Sequences and Series
summary: An arithmetic progression (AP) adds a fixed common difference d; a geometric progression (GP) multiplies by a fixed ratio r. Harmonic progression (HP) is the reciprocal of an AP.
Know the nth term and sum formulas, the sum of an infinite GP (|r| < 1), and the means AM, GM, HM with AM ≥ GM ≥ HM for positive numbers.
Special series: Σn, Σn², Σn³, arithmetico-geometric progressions (AGP) and telescoping (method of differences) are frequent in JEE.

formulas.name: AP properties
formulas.formula: three terms in AP: a − d, a, a + d;  if a, b, c in AP then 2b = a + c;  tₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁

formulas.name: HP
formulas.formula: a, b, c in HP ⇔ 1/a, 1/b, 1/c in AP;  b = 2ac/(a + c)
formulas.note: There is no formula for the sum of an HP.

formulas.name: Means
formulas.formula: AM = (a + b)/2;  GM = √(ab);  HM = 2ab/(a + b);  GM² = AM × HM

formulas.name: AM–GM–HM inequality
formulas.formula: AM ≥ GM ≥ HM (equality iff all numbers equal)

formulas.name: Inserting means
formulas.formula: n AMs between a and b: d = (b − a)/(n + 1);  n GMs: r = (b/a)^(1/(n + 1))

formulas.name: nth term from differences
formulas.formula: if successive differences of the terms form an AP, tₙ is quadratic in n; if they form a GP, tₙ = arⁿ + b
formulas.when: Finding the general term of unusual series.

examples.title: Means of 4 and 16
examples.problem: Find AM, GM and HM of 4 and 16.
examples.solution: AM = 10, GM = 8, HM = 6.4; check GM² = AM × HM: 64 = 10 × 6.4.

examples.title: Minimum using AM–GM
examples.problem: Find the minimum of x + 9/x for x > 0.

topics.title: Choosing terms
topics.explain: For AP with known sum use a − d, a, a + d (three terms) or a − 3d, a − d, a + d, a + 3d (four terms). For GP use a/r, a, ar.

topics.title: Properties of AP and GP
topics.explain: Adding, subtracting, multiplying or dividing every term of an AP by a constant keeps it an AP (except division by 0). Multiplying terms of a GP by a constant keeps it a GP; reciprocals of a GP also form a GP; logs of a GP form an AP.

topics.title: Sum of n terms from Sₙ
topics.explain: If Sₙ is given as a function of n, then tₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ (n ≥ 2), t₁ = S₁. A quadratic Sₙ without constant term means AP.

topics.title: Relation between AM, GM, HM
topics.explain: For positive a, b: A ≥ G ≥ H, G² = AH. The numbers a and b are roots of x² − 2Ax + G² = 0.

topics.title: Series to recognise
topics.explain: 1 + 11 + 111 + … — write 111…1 = (10ⁿ − 1)/9. 0.7 + 0.77 + 0.777 + … — similar trick. Sum of products like 1·2 + 2·3 + … = Σn² + Σn.

topics.title: Weighted AM–GM
topics.explain: For positive numbers with weights, weighted AM ≥ weighted GM. Used for maximising products under a sum constraint, e.g. maximise x²y³ given x + y = 5.

ratta: GP: tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹;  S∞ = a/(1 − r).
HP: reciprocals in AP; b = 2ac/(a + c).
